chunk: Training & Development Policy (EN, 202501) # Training & Development Policy

The Training & Development Policy outlines the commitment of Global Service Firm to foster a culture of continuous learning and professional growth. This policy applies to all employees globally and aims to enhance individual and organizational capabilities through structured training and development initiatives.

1. Continuous Learning: We believe in the importance of lifelong learning to adapt to changing business environments and individual career aspirations. 2. Fairness: Training opportunities will be provided equitably to all employees, ensuring that everyone has access to the resources they need for professional growth. 3. Accessibility: Training programs will be designed to accommodate diverse learning styles and needs, ensuring that all employees can participate. 4. Return on Investment (ROI): We will assess the effectiveness of training programs to ensure that they contribute positively to both employee performance and organizational goals. 5. Innovation: We encourage innovative approaches to training and development, including the use of technology and new learning methodologies.

Employees: Actively engage in their own development by identifying training needs and participating in available programs. Managers: Support employees in their development by facilitating access to training resources and encouraging participation. HR Team: Oversee the implementation of the Training & Development Policy, ensuring compliance and alignment with organizational goals. L&D Team: Design and deliver training programs, evaluate their effectiveness, and recommend improvements. Executives: Champion a culture of learning and allocate necessary resources to support training initiatives.

All fulltime and parttime employees are eligible for training and development opportunities. Budget allocation for training will be based on departmental needs and individual development plans, with a focus on strategic alignment with company objectives.

Mandatory training programs include: 1. Compliance Training: Required for all employees to ensure adherence to legal and regulatory standards. 2. Security Training: Essential for safeguarding company data and assets. 3. Onboarding Training: Designed for new hires to familiarize them with company policies, culture, and expectations. 4. Health & Safety Training: Required for all employees to promote a safe working environment.

Optional training opportunities include: 1. Professional Skills Development: Workshops and courses aimed at enhancing jobrelated skills. 2. Certifications: Financial support for obtaining industryrecognized certifications. 3. Conferences: Opportunities to attend industry events for networking and knowledge sharing.

Training may be delivered in various formats, including: Online Learning: Selfpaced modules accessible through the company’s Learning Management System (LMS). Classroom Training: Instructorled sessions held onsite or at external venues. Blended Learning: A combination of online and classroombased training. Mentoring: Oneonone guidance from experienced colleagues. OntheJob Training: Handson experience under the supervision of skilled team members.

1. Individual Development Plans (IDPs): Employees will work with their managers to create personalized development plans that align with career goals. 2. Leadership Tracks: Programs designed to prepare highpotential employees for leadership roles within the organization. 3. Succession Planning: Identifying and developing internal talent to fill key positions in the future.

Limits: Each employee may access a designated budget for training annually, subject to departmental approval. Annual Caps: A maximum cap will be set for training expenses based on role levels, as outlined in the table below. Carryover Rules: Unused training budgets may be carried over to the next fiscal year, subject to managerial approval. | Role Level | Annual Training Budget Limit | ||| | EntryLevel | $1,000 | | MidLevel | $1,500 | | SeniorLevel | $2,500 | | ExecutiveLevel | $5,000 |

Employees seeking reimbursement for external training must: 1. Submit a training request form to their manager for approval. 2. Provide proof of payment and completion upon finishing the training. 3. Submit receipts to HR for reimbursement within 30 days of completion.

subsection: Process for Requesting and Approving Training
chunk: 1. Request Submission: Employees submit a training request form detailing the training program, objectives, and expected outcomes. 2. Manager Review: Managers review the request, considering alignment with departmental goals and budget availability. 3. Approval Process: Approved requests are forwarded to the HR team for final confirmation and budget allocation.

Training programs will be evaluated through: Feedback Surveys: Participants will provide feedback on training content, delivery, and relevance. Performance Impact: Assessment of changes in employee performance posttraining. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs): Metrics will be established to measure the effectiveness of training initiatives.
Training and development will be integrated into the performance review process. Employees will discuss their training experiences and future development needs during annual performance evaluations.
The HR team will maintain records of all training activities, including: Employee participation and completion rates. Feedback and evaluation results. Budget expenditures.
All training programs will comply with applicable regional and global regulations, ensuring that Global Service Firm meets legal obligations and industry standards.

subsection: Example Scenario: Employee Requests Certification Training
chunk: Scenario: An employee in the IT department wishes to pursue a certification in cloud computing. 1. The employee completes a training request form, outlining the certification program and its relevance to their current role. 2. The employee’s manager reviews the request, considers the departmental budget, and approves it, highlighting the potential benefits for the team. 3. The HR team confirms the budget allocation and informs the employee of the next steps for reimbursement upon completion.

subsection: Example Flow: Manager Approves Team Training
chunk: 1. A manager identifies a need for team training in project management. 2. The manager submits a training request form for a group workshop, detailing the expected outcomes and benefits. 3. The HR team reviews the request, approves the budget, and schedules the training session.

subsection: Checklist for Employees Before Submitting a Training Request
chunk: [ ] Identify the training program and its objectives. [ ] Assess how the training aligns with career goals. [ ] Confirm budget availability with your manager. [ ] Complete the training request form accurately. [ ] Submit the request in advance of the training date.

L&D (Learning and Development): A function within HR focused on employee training and development. IDP (Individual Development Plan): A customized plan outlining an employee's career goals and the training needed to achieve them. ROI (Return on Investment): A measure of the profitability of training programs.

1. What types of training are mandatory? Compliance, security, onboarding, and health & safety training are mandatory for all employees. 2. How do I request training? Complete a training request form and submit it to your manager for approval. 3. Is there a budget for training? Yes, each employee has an annual training budget based on their role level. 4. Can I carry over unused training budget? Yes, unused budgets may be carried over to the next fiscal year with managerial approval. 5. How is training effectiveness evaluated? Through feedback surveys, performance impact assessments, and KPIs. 6. What if my training request is denied? You may discuss the reasons with your manager and explore alternative training options. 7. Are there opportunities for leadership development? Yes, we offer leadership tracks and succession planning programs. 8. How can I find available training programs? Check the company’s Learning Management System (LMS) for a list of available training opportunities. 9. What happens if I don’t complete the training? Uncompleted training may impact your performance review and development plan. 10. Can I attend external conferences? Yes, with prior approval, you may attend conferences relevant to your role and development goals. This Training & Development Policy is designed to support the growth and success of our employees and the organization as a whole.
